idiom_name: discriminated union of node interfaces with a shared children field
implementation_notes: TypeScript models the node set as a discriminated union: one interface per node kind with a literal type tag, its node-specific data, and a shared readonly children member, so a generic walker over children type-checks against the union and per-node dispatch is a switch on the tag with exhaustiveness checked by assigning the remaining case to never. ESTree is the community specification of exactly this node shape for JavaScript tooling, which makes the union form the ecosystem default. Build the children array and the named fields from one place - the constructor - so the two views cannot drift apart.
pitfalls: The children array and the named fields are independent properties: nothing stops left/right from disagreeing with children[0]/children[1] unless both are built in one constructor.
Exhaustiveness via never only works while the union is closed in one compilation unit and no default arm exists; adding a node interface later silently re-enables the switch.
readonly is erased at runtime: cached traversals keyed by identity can be invalidated by code that mutates the arrays anyway.
